text:
Maya: Heads up — noticed a sharp jump in EventSource tail latency after this morning's rollout. 95th/99th spiked around 09:30 UTC. Dashboard -> https://grafana.redwood/streams/evt-latency
Jin: yep, perf-ci alerted me too. Which PR landed this morning? :eyes:
perf-ci-bot: perf/regressions job #482 failed on staging — regression flagged: SSE median and 95th increased for tool-call flows at commit 2f7a9c1
Omar: I started a local bisect, looks like commit 2f7a9c1 (PR #3421) is the culprit. It changed EventSource framing for tool-calls: switched from raw JSON chunks to base64-wrapped payloads to fix client interop.
Casey: base64 on the hot path? That will add CPU and allocs. Any other changes in that PR?
Omar: PR also normalized KV cache keys for toolcall requests (lowercase + strip). Both changes landed together. Snippet from PR:
```
- stream.write(chunk)
+ const buf = Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(chunk))
+ stream.write(buf.toString('base64'))
```
Priya: key normalization could affect KV cache hit-rate. Combined with base64 decode per frame we might see both more CPU and lower cache hits.
Maya: timeline — both changes in same PR? That makes bisecting a bit trickier but at least we know where to start.
Jin: replayed production traces against staging with the PR. Baseline 95th was ~120ms; after PR 95th jumped to ~260ms for toolcall SSE. CPU profile shows ~18% more time in Buffer.toString and JSON.parse.
Casey: can we revert encoding change only and keep the key normalization? Quick revert candidate: `git revert 2f7a9c1 --no-commit` then drop the encoding hunk.
Maya: deploy-bot, can we canary revert to staging (small traffic slice)?
deploy-bot: starting canary revert of commit 2f7a9c1 to staging (canary 5% traffic). Deploy started 2026-03-18T11:05Z.
Priya: if we revert encoding but keep key normalization, add a probe to measure KV cache hit/miss by route — want to see immediate impact.
Omar: canary results: 95th down to ~130ms (close to baseline). KV hit-rate dropped ~4% vs pre-change, but CPU decode overhead explained majority of latency regression.
Jin: recommendation: revert the whole PR in prod, then rework framing (length-prefixed binary or explicit boundary frames) rather than base64; and add a compatibility shim for kvcache keys. I'm +1 for rollback to stop user impact.
Casey: agreed. Post-rollback plan: (1) design binary framing for EventSource that avoids base64/JSON roundtrip; (2) microbench base64 path vs direct write; (3) add kvcache compatibility shim to avoid immediate hit loss.
Maya: filing rollback RFC and opening the revert PR now. Action items: Maya -> coordinate prod revert; Priya -> kvcache probe + regression test for normalization; Omar -> prototype length-prefixed framing + bench; Jin -> add perf CI job to replay toolcall SSE traces.
deploy-bot: revert PR #3421 deployed to prod (2026-03-18T11:42Z) — routing back to normal.
Jin: post-rollback metrics look good: 95th back to expected, CPU tail reduced. Leaving kvcache probe on overnight to watch for latent issues.
Priya: created follow-ups: PERF-789 (EventSource framing redesign), KVC-132 (kvcache compatibility shim), CI-201 (SSE replay perf job).
Maya: thanks all. Revert successful — will follow up on design work. :white_check_mark:
